competition_title: STAT 303 Chapter 2: Project Environments, Packages, and File Paths

questions.title: You want to run the shell command cd data, but the terminal prompt is >>>. What should you do first?
options: Type cd data after >>>
Type exit() to return to the shell
Create another virtual environment
Restart the notebook kernel

questions.title: A terminal and a running notebook both start in stat303-setup. You run cd data only in the terminal. What happens?
options: Both working directories change to stat303-setup/data
The CSV file moves into the notebook folder
The terminal stays in stat303-setup until the notebook restarts
Only the terminal working directory changes

questions.title: Two projects need incompatible versions of the same library. How do separate virtual environments help?
options: Each project can keep its own compatible package versions
They make incompatible versions work together inside one environment
They force both projects to use the newest library version
They remove the need to install packages

questions.title: On macOS, a terminal uses /course/A/.venv/bin/python, but the notebook uses /course/B/.venv/bin/python. A terminal package installation succeeds and the notebook import fails. What should you check first?
options: Whether both environments are named .venv
Whether the CSV is in the data folder
Whether both use the intended project’s Python executable
Whether the notebook has been exported to HTML

questions.title: In the project folder, python -m venv .venv succeeds using an installed Python. What should you expect?
options: It downloads the newest Python release and all course packages
It creates an environment based on that Python; course packages still need installation
It copies every package from every other environment
It automatically makes all existing notebooks use the new environment

questions.title: Pandas is installed in the selected project environment. You restart the notebook kernel. What is normally needed before using pd again?
options: Create a new .venv folder
Install Pandas again
Copy Pandas into the notebook folder
Rerun import pandas as pd

questions.title: You run %pip install seaborn in a VS Code notebook code cell. Which environment receives Seaborn?
options: The environment used by the notebook’s selected kernel
Every Python environment on the computer
The environment used by any open terminal
The folder containing the CSV file

questions.title: A classmate has created and activated a new compatible environment and received your requirements.txt. Which command installs its listed packages?
options: python -m pip freeze
python -m venv requirements.txt
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python requirements.txt

questions.title: A project contains sibling folders notebooks and data. The CSV is in data. If the notebook’s current working directory is project/notebooks, which path reaches the CSV? Assume Path has been imported from pathlib.
options: Path("data") / "station_readings.csv"
Path("..") / "data" / "station_readings.csv"
Path("notebooks") / "data" / "station_readings.csv"
Path("station_readings.csv")

questions.title: For data_path = Path("data") / "station_readings.csv", resolve() displays an absolute path but is_file() returns False. What is the best next step?
options: Use resolve() again to create the missing CSV
Assume the file exists because the path is absolute
Reinstall Pandas before checking the folders
Check Path.cwd(), the filename, capitalization, and folder layout
